name: Learn basic pen spinning
blurb: Three fundamental spins — ThumbAround, Charge and Sonic — cover most of what looks impressive, and you can practise them in any meeting for the rest of your life.
gear: A slightly weighted pen, or a modified one with caps on both ends
A carpet or lap to drop onto
steps: Build or buy a spinning pen: a longer, heavier pen with balanced ends is dramatically easier than a standard biro.
Learn the ThumbAround: push the pen with your middle finger so it rotates once around your thumb, and catch it between index and middle.
Learn the Charge: rotate the pen continuously in the gap between two fingers, driven by small circles from your wrist.
Learn the Sonic: the pen passes rapidly between fingers in a flicking pass.
Practise each 100 times a day, alternating hands, and accept a fortnight of dropping.
Link two spins into a combo with a clean transition.
tips: Practise sitting down with the pen over your lap so drops do not interrupt the rhythm.
Learn on your dominant hand first, then port each trick over — the second hand goes much faster.
proof: You perform a ThumbAround into a second trick, ten times in a row, without a drop.
